name: QuantumParallelRepetition.posSemidef_blockDiagonal'
theorem_title: Block diagonal matrices with positive semidefinite blocks are positive semidefinite
natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set and, for each $j \in \iota$, let $d_j$ be a finite set and
$M_j \in \mathbb{C}^{d_j \times d_j}$ a square complex matrix. Form the block diagonal matrix
$\bigoplus_{j \in \iota} M_j$ acting on $\bigoplus_{j \in \iota} \mathbb{C}^{d_j}$, indexed by the
dependent sum $\Sigma_{j}\, d_j$: its $((j,r),(k,s))$ entry is $(M_j)_{rs}$ when $j = k$ and $0$
otherwise. If every block $M_j$ is positive semidefinite, then $\bigoplus_j M_j$ is positive
semidefinite. This is the dependently typed version of the statement, in which the blocks are
allowed to have different sizes.
explanation:
Since each $M_j$ is positive semidefinite, it is a nonnegative element of the $C^*$-algebra
$\mathbb{C}^{d_j \times d_j}$, hence factors as $M_j = K_j^{*} K_j$ for some $K_j$
(`CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self`); choose such a family $(K_j)_j$. Block
diagonalization is a $*$-homomorphism: it commutes with taking adjoints and with multiplication
(`Matrix.blockDiagonal'_mul`), so
$\bigoplus_j M_j = \bigoplus_j K_j^{*}K_j = \bigl(\bigoplus_j K_j\bigr)^{*}\bigl(\bigoplus_j
K_j\bigr)$. A matrix of the form $A^{*}A$ is nonnegative, and nonnegativity in the matrix
$C^*$-algebra is exactly positive semidefiniteness.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.mixtureEmbedding_isometry
theorem_title: The matched index embedding of a family of strategies is an isometry
natural_language_statement:
Let $(S_j)_{j \in J}$ be a finite family of strategies for a game $G$, where $S_j$ has local
systems $\mathcal{A}_j$ for Alice and $\mathcal{B}_j$ for Bob. Write
$\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_j \mathcal{A}_j$ and $\mathcal{B} = \bigsqcup_j \mathcal{B}_j$ for the
index sets of the direct sums, and let $\mathcal{M} = \bigsqcup_j (\mathcal{A}_j \times
\mathcal{B}_j)$ be the set of *matched* triples $(j,a,b)$, i.e. those pairs of basis vectors of
$\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}$ that live in the same block. Let $V$ be the $0/1$ matrix with rows
indexed by $\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}$ and columns by $\mathcal{M}$ whose $(q, r)$ entry is
$1$ exactly when $q$ is the pair of coordinates determined by the matched triple $r$. Then
$V^{\dagger} V = I$, so $V$ is an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^{\mathcal{M}}$ into
$\mathbb{C}^{\mathcal{A}} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{\mathcal{B}}$.
explanation:
The identity is checked entrywise. The $(r,r)$ entry of $V^{\dagger}V$ counts the rows where the
$r$-th column of $V$ is nonzero; that column is the single standard basis vector indexed by the
matched pair attached to $r$, so the entry is $1$. For $r \neq r'$ the two columns are supported on
distinct basis vectors, because the map sending a matched triple $(j,a,b)$ to the pair
$((j,a),(j,b))$ is injective, so the inner product vanishes; `simp` with the definition of matrix
multiplication and of the conjugate transpose closes both cases.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.mixtureBlockMatrix_posSemidef
theorem_title: The block diagonal mixture of strategy states is positive semidefinite
natural_language_statement:
Let $(S_j)_{j \in J}$ be a finite family of strategies for a game $G$, with shared bipartite states
$\rho_j$ on $\mathcal{A}_j \otimes \mathcal{B}_j$, and let $p : J \to \mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative
weights. The mixture block matrix is the block diagonal matrix $\bigoplus_{j \in J} p_j \rho_j$ on
the matched index set $\bigsqcup_j (\mathcal{A}_j \times \mathcal{B}_j)$. Then this matrix is
positive semidefinite. No normalization of $p$ is assumed; only $p_j \ge 0$ is needed.
explanation:
The proof is a reduction to the platform theorem that a block diagonal matrix all of whose blocks
are positive semidefinite is itself positive semidefinite
(`QuantumParallelRepetition.posSemidef_blockDiagonal'`). After unfolding the mixture block matrix
to its block diagonal form, it suffices to check each block: $p_j \rho_j$ is a nonnegative real
multiple of the density matrix $\rho_j$, which is positive semidefinite, and positive
semidefiniteness is preserved under scaling by a nonnegative scalar.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.mixtureBlockMatrix_trace
theorem_title: Trace of the block diagonal mixture matrix is the total weight
natural_language_statement:
Let $(S_j)_{j \in J}$ be a finite family of strategies for a game $G$ with shared states $\rho_j$,
and let $p : J \to \mathbb{R}$ be arbitrary real weights (no sign or normalization condition). The
block diagonal matrix $\bigoplus_{j \in J} p_j \rho_j$ has trace
$$\operatorname{tr}\Bigl(\bigoplus_{j \in J} p_j \rho_j\Bigr) = \sum_{j \in J} p_j,$$
the right-hand side being read as a complex number via the inclusion $\mathbb{R} \hookrightarrow
\mathbb{C}$. Together with the positivity statement, this says the mixture matrix is a density
matrix precisely when the weights are nonnegative and sum to $1$.
explanation:
The trace of a block diagonal matrix is the sum of the traces of its blocks
(`Matrix.trace_blockDiagonal'`). Each block contributes $\operatorname{tr}(p_j \rho_j) = p_j
\operatorname{tr}(\rho_j) = p_j$, since the trace is linear and a density matrix has unit trace
(`DensityMatrix.trace_one`). Summing over $j$ and pushing the coercion $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$
through the finite sum gives the claim.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.purifiedRefinedEffect_posSemidef
theorem_title: Purified refined effects are positive semidefinite
natural_language_statement:
Let $F \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ be positive semidefinite and let $F^{+}$ denote its spectral
pseudo-inverse, obtained by inverting the nonzero eigenvalues of $F$ and leaving its kernel
untouched. Let $\Gamma \in \mathbb{C}^{e \times d}$ satisfy $\Gamma^{\dagger}\Gamma = F$, so that
$\Gamma$ is a dilation of $F$, and write $P = \Gamma F^{+} \Gamma^{\dagger}$. Given a finite family
$(M_a)_{a \in \iota}$ of positive semidefinite matrices on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$ and a distinguished
index $a_0$, define the purified refined effects on $\mathbb{C}^{e}$ by
$$E_a \;=\; \Gamma F^{+} M_a F^{+} \Gamma^{\dagger} \;+\; \mathbf{1}[a = a_0]\,\bigl(I - P\bigr).$$
Then every $E_a$ is positive semidefinite. This is the positivity half of the assertion that the
$E_a$ form a POVM on the dilation space, the completeness half being proved separately.
explanation:
Split $E_a$ into its two summands and use that a sum of positive semidefinite matrices is positive
semidefinite. The core term is positive semidefinite because $F^{+}$ is Hermitian, so
$\Gamma F^{+} M_a F^{+}\Gamma^{\dagger} = C^{\dagger} M_a C$ with $C = F^{+}\Gamma^{\dagger}$, and
conjugation preserves positivity; this is packaged as `purifiedRefinementCore_posSemidef`. The
correction term is either $0$ or $I - P$, and the hypothesis $\Gamma^{\dagger}\Gamma = F$ makes $P$
an idempotent Hermitian matrix, i.e. an orthogonal projection, whence $I - P \succeq 0$
(`purificationRangeProjection_complement_posSemidef`).

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.purifiedRefinedEffect_complete
theorem_title: Purified refined effects sum to the identity
natural_language_statement:
Let $F \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ be positive semidefinite with spectral pseudo-inverse $F^{+}$,
let $\Gamma \in \mathbb{C}^{e \times d}$ be arbitrary, and set $P = \Gamma F^{+}\Gamma^{\dagger}$.
Suppose the finite family $(M_a)_{a \in \iota}$ of matrices on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$ resolves $F$, that
is $\sum_{a} M_a = F$. Then the purified refined effects
$E_a = \Gamma F^{+} M_a F^{+}\Gamma^{\dagger} + \mathbf{1}[a = a_0]\,(I - P)$ satisfy
$$\sum_{a \in \iota} E_a = I_{e}$$
for every choice of distinguished index $a_0$. Combined with their positivity, this exhibits
$(E_a)_{a}$ as a POVM on $\mathbb{C}^{e}$, the deficiency $I - P$ being dumped on the single
outcome $a_0$.
explanation:
Split the sum over $a$ into the sum of core terms and the sum of correction terms. The core terms
telescope by linearity: $\sum_a \Gamma F^{+} M_a F^{+}\Gamma^{\dagger} = \Gamma F^{+} F F^{+}
\Gamma^{\dagger} = \Gamma F^{+}\Gamma^{\dagger} = P$, using $\sum_a M_a = F$ and the pseudo-inverse
identity $F^{+}FF^{+} = F^{+}$; this is the auxiliary lemma `purifiedRefinementCore_sum`. Exactly
one correction term is nonzero, contributing $I - P$, so the total is $P + (I - P) = I$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.fullSubsetHistory_mass_eq_postselection
theorem_title: Subset history expansion computes the probability of winning every coordinate of $D$
natural_language_statement:
Fix a game $G$ with question distribution $\mu$ on $X \times Y$ and marginals $\mu_X, \mu_Y$, an
integer $n$, a strategy $S$ for the $n$-fold repetition $G^{\otimes n}$ with shared state $\rho$,
and two coordinate sets $D, L \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$ with $L \cap D = \emptyset$; write
$R = \{1,\dots,n\} \setminus (D \cup L)$. A *full subset history* $h$ records the question pair
$(x_i,y_i)$ for $i \in D$, Alice's question $x_i$ for $i \in L$, and Bob's question $y_i$ for
$i \in R$, and carries the weight
$w(h) = \prod_{i \in D}\mu(x_i,y_i)\prod_{i \in L}\mu_X(x_i)\prod_{i \in R}\mu_Y(y_i)$.
For answer tuples $\alpha \in A^{D}$, $\beta \in B^{D}$ let $[h,\alpha,\beta] \in \{0,1\}$ be the
indicator that the verifier accepts at every coordinate of $D$, and let $A_{h,\alpha}$ and
$B_{h,\beta}$ be the players' *filters*: Alice's measurement operator for answering $\alpha$ on $D$
(and anything elsewhere), averaged over her unseen questions on $R$ with the conditional law
$\mu(x \mid y)$, and symmetrically for Bob over his unseen questions on $L$ with
$\mu(y \mid x)$. Then
$$\sum_{h}\sum_{\alpha \in A^{D}}\sum_{\beta \in B^{D}} w(h)\,[h,\alpha,\beta]\;
\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(A_{h,\alpha}\otimes B_{h,\beta})\bigr)
\;=\; \Pr\bigl[\text{the players win at every coordinate } i \in D\bigr],$$
the right-hand side being the mass of the event $\{\forall i \in D:\ V(x_i,y_i,a_i,b_i)\}$ under
the law on $(x,y,a,b)$ induced by $\mu^{\otimes n}$ and $S$. Thus the history decomposition, which
hides half of each player's questions, computes exactly the postselection probability of winning
the coordinates in $D$.
explanation:
The proof is a chain of rewrites. First expand each filter pair inside the Born pairing, using
bilinearity of $(F,G)\mapsto \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,(F \otimes G))$, into a
double sum over the hidden question tuples $x_R$ and $y_L$ of the conditioned effects
(`fullHistoryFilters_born_expansion`); then reorder the resulting five nested finite sums. Next,
`fullHistoryWeight_mul_hidden` shows that the history weight times the two hidden conditional
weights is exactly the product question weight $\mu^{\otimes n}(x,y)$ of the reconstructed question
pair, and `fullHistoryWinIndicator_eq_question` shows the history win indicator agrees with the one
read off the reconstructed questions; here the hypothesis $L \subseteq D^{c}$ is what makes the
reconstruction consistent. Summing over histories together with the hidden data is then a
reindexing along the bijection between (history, hidden questions) and full question pairs
$(x,y)$, so the expression collapses to
$\sum_{x,y}\mu^{\otimes n}(x,y)\sum_{\alpha,\beta}[\,\cdot\,]\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}
(\rho\,(A_{\alpha,x}\otimes B_{\beta,y}))$. A final lemma
(`fullQuestionConditionedBornMass_eq`) identifies this with the event mass of the win event on $D$
under the strategy's outcome law, by summing the Born rule over the answers unconstrained on
$D^{c}$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.scalarResolventFilter_memLp_two
theorem_title: The scalar resolvent filter $s \mapsto z/(z+s)$ lies in $L^2(0,\infty)$
natural_language_statement:
For every real $z \ge 0$, the function
$$s \;\longmapsto\; \frac{z}{z+s}, \qquad s \in (0,\infty),$$
belongs to $L^{2}\bigl((0,\infty), \mathrm{d}s\bigr)$: it is almost everywhere strongly measurable
and $\int_{0}^{\infty} \bigl(z/(z+s)\bigr)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s < \infty$ (the integral in fact equals
$z$). For $z = 0$ the function vanishes identically. This is the scalar model for the matrix valued
purification filter $F \mapsto F(F+s)^{-1}$, applied one eigenvalue at a time.
explanation:
Measurability is immediate: the integrand is a quotient of a constant by the continuous, nowhere
vanishing function $s \mapsto z + s$ on $(0,\infty)$, so it is measurable and hence almost
everywhere strongly measurable. For $p = 2$, membership in $L^{p}$ is equivalent to integrability
of the square (`memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq`), and that integrability is the auxiliary estimate
`scalar_resolvent_purification_integrable`, which handles $z = 0$ trivially and for $z > 0$
integrates the tail $z^{2}(z+s)^{-2}$ explicitly.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.spectralPurificationFilter_memLp_two
theorem_title: The spectral purification filter is square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$
natural_language_statement:
Let $F \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ be positive semidefinite with spectral decomposition
$F = U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d)U^{\dagger}$, where $U$ is unitary and
$\lambda_i \ge 0$. Define the matrix valued *spectral purification filter*
$$\Phi_F(s) \;=\; U\,\operatorname{diag}\!\Bigl(\frac{\lambda_i}{\lambda_i+s}\Bigr)\,U^{\dagger},
\qquad s \in (0,\infty),$$
which is the resolvent expression $F(F+s)^{-1}$ read off the spectrum. Then $\Phi_F$ belongs to
$L^{2}\bigl((0,\infty),\mathrm{d}s\bigr)$ as a function valued in the finite-dimensional normed
space of $d \times d$ matrices; equivalently, every matrix entry $s \mapsto (\Phi_F(s))_{ij}$ is
square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$.
explanation:
The proof is a reduction to the scalar case, namely the platform theorem
`QuantumParallelRepetition.scalarResolventFilter_memLp_two` that $s \mapsto z/(z+s)$ is in $L^{2}$
for $z \ge 0$. Since the target is a finite product of copies of $\mathbb{C}$, $L^{2}$ membership
can be checked entrywise (`MemLp.of_eval` applied twice). Expanding the conjugation gives
$(\Phi_F(s))_{ij} = \sum_{k} U_{ik}\,\frac{\lambda_k}{\lambda_k+s}\,\overline{U_{jk}}$, a finite sum
of constant multiples of scalar resolvent filters at the eigenvalues $\lambda_k$, which are
nonnegative because $F$ is positive semidefinite. Finite sums and multiplication by constants
preserve $L^{2}$ membership (`memLp_finsetSum`), which gives the claim.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.positiveMatrixSpectralAtom_posSemidef
theorem_title: Spectral atoms of a positive semidefinite matrix are positive semidefinite
natural_language_statement:
Let $F \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ be positive semidefinite and let $U$ be the unitary whose
columns form the orthonormal eigenbasis of $F$ supplied by the spectral theorem. For an index
$i \in d$, define the *spectral atom* $P_i = U E_{ii} U^{\dagger}$, where $E_{ii}$ is the diagonal
matrix with a single $1$ in position $i$ and zeros elsewhere. Then $P_i$ is positive semidefinite.
Concretely $P_i$ is the rank one orthogonal projection onto the $i$-th eigenvector of $F$.
explanation:
The diagonal matrix $E_{ii}$ is positive semidefinite because each of its diagonal entries is $0$
or $1$, hence nonnegative (`Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal`, checked by splitting on whether the
diagonal index equals $i$). Positive semidefiniteness is preserved by congruence: for any $M$,
$M N M^{\dagger} \succeq 0$ whenever $N \succeq 0$ (`Matrix.PosSemidef.mul_mul_conjTranspose_same`).
Unfolding the spectral conjugation map to $X \mapsto U X U^{\dagger}$ and applying this with
$M = U$ and $N = E_{ii}$ gives the result.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.positiveMatrixSpectralAtom_sum
theorem_title: Spectral atoms of a positive semidefinite matrix resolve the identity
natural_language_statement:
Let $F \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}$ be positive semidefinite with eigenvector unitary $U$, and let
$P_i = U E_{ii} U^{\dagger}$ be its spectral atoms, where $E_{ii}$ is the diagonal matrix with a
single $1$ in position $i$. Then
$$\sum_{i \in d} P_i \;=\; I_d.$$
Together with the positivity of each $P_i$, this says the spectral atoms form a resolution of the
identity, so they may be used as a projective measurement adapted to $F$.
explanation:
The conjugation $X \mapsto U X U^{\dagger}$ is a linear map, so the sum may be pushed inside
(`map_sum`). The diagonal matrices $E_{ii}$ sum to the identity, checked entrywise: a diagonal
entry receives exactly one contribution of $1$ and an off-diagonal entry receives none. Hence the
total equals $U I U^{\dagger} = U U^{\dagger} = I$ by unitarity of $U$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.matrixLogEntropy_born_lower_bound_left
theorem_title: Operator entropy of an effect is bounded by the entropy of its Born mass
natural_language_statement:
Let $\rho$ be a density matrix on $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ with $\mathcal{H}_A,
\mathcal{H}_B$ finite dimensional, and write
$\langle F, G\rangle_{\rho} = \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(F \otimes G)\bigr)$
for the Born pairing. Let $F$ be an effect on $A$, i.e. $0 \preceq F \preceq I$, and $G$ an effect
on $B$, i.e. $0 \preceq G \preceq I$. Let $\eta(t) = -t\log t$ and let $F\log F$ be defined by the
continuous functional calculus. Then
$$-\bigl\langle F\log F,\; G\bigr\rangle_{\rho} \;\le\; \eta\bigl(\langle F, G\rangle_{\rho}\bigr).$$
In words: the operator entropy of the effect $F$, measured against $G$ in the state $\rho$, never
exceeds the scalar entropy of the total Born mass $\langle F, G\rangle_{\rho}$ that the pair
$(F,G)$ collects. This is the one-sided ("left", i.e. $F$ on Alice's factor) entropy estimate used
to control the information cost of conditioning on a measurement outcome.
explanation:
Decompose along the spectral atoms $P_i$ of $F$: setting $w_i = \langle P_i, G\rangle_{\rho}$ and
letting $\lambda_i$ be the eigenvalues of $F$, one has $w_i \ge 0$, $\sum_i w_i = \langle I,
G\rangle_{\rho}$, $\sum_i w_i \lambda_i = \langle F, G\rangle_{\rho}$ and
$-\langle F\log F, G\rangle_{\rho} = \sum_i w_i\,\eta(\lambda_i)$
(`leftSpectralBornWeight_moment`, `leftSpectralBornWeight_negEntropy`). Nonnegativity of these
pairings comes from the imported platform theorem
`QuantumParallelRepetition.trace_mul_posSemidef_nonneg`, that the trace of a product of positive
semidefinite matrices is nonnegative, applied to $\rho$ and $P_i \otimes G$. The hypotheses
$F \preceq I$ and $G \preceq I$ give $\lambda_i \in [0,1]$ and total weight $\sum_i w_i \le 1$.
If the Born mass $p = \langle F, G\rangle_{\rho}$ is $0$ then every term $w_i\lambda_i$ vanishes,
forcing $\sum_i w_i \eta(\lambda_i) = 0$ and both sides are $0$; otherwise the claim is exactly the
scalar weighted entropy bound $\sum_i w_i\,\eta(\lambda_i) \le p\log(1/p)$ for nonnegative weights
of total mass at most $1$ (`finite_weighted_entropy_le_of_weight_bound`), and
$p\log(1/p) = \eta(p)$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.embezzlementState_norm
theorem_title: The normalized embezzlement state is a unit vector
natural_language_statement:
For $n \ge 1$ let
$$|\mu_n^{\mathrm{raw}}\rangle \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac{1}{\sqrt{j}}\;|j\rangle \otimes |j\rangle
\;\in\; \mathbb{C}^{n}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{n}$$
be the unnormalized van Dam-Hayden harmonic state, and let
$|\mu_n\rangle = \bigl\||\mu_n^{\mathrm{raw}}\rangle\bigr\|^{-1}\,|\mu_n^{\mathrm{raw}}\rangle$ be
its normalization (so $\||\mu_n^{\mathrm{raw}}\rangle\|^{2}$ is the harmonic number $H_n$). Then
$\bigl\||\mu_n\rangle\bigr\| = 1$. The hypothesis $n > 0$ is needed only to guarantee that the raw
vector is nonzero, so that dividing by its norm is legitimate.
explanation:
For $n > 0$ the raw state is nonzero (it has a nonzero entry at $(1,1)$), hence its norm is a
nonzero real number (`rawEmbezzlementState_ne_zero`). Unfolding the definition and using
homogeneity of the norm under real scalar multiplication, $\|c\,v\| = |c|\,\|v\|$ with
$c = \|v\|^{-1} > 0$, the absolute value can be dropped and the product cancels
(`inv_mul_cancel`), leaving $1$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.diagonalSchmidtState_norm_sq
theorem_title: Squared norm of a diagonal Schmidt state is the sum of the squared coefficients
natural_language_statement:
Let $d$ be a finite index set and $\sigma : d \to \mathbb{R}$ a family of real coefficients. Let
$$|\psi_\sigma\rangle \;=\; \sum_{i \in d} \sigma_i\;|i\rangle \otimes |i\rangle$$
be the corresponding diagonal state in the Euclidean space $\ell^{2}(d \times d)$, whose entry at
$(i,j)$ is $\sigma_i$ if $i = j$ and $0$ otherwise. Then
$$\bigl\||\psi_\sigma\rangle\bigr\|^{2} \;=\; \sum_{i \in d} \sigma_i^{2}.$$
In particular $|\psi_\sigma\rangle$ is a unit vector exactly when $\sum_i \sigma_i^{2} = 1$, which
is the condition for the $\sigma_i$ to be Schmidt coefficients of a bipartite unit vector.
explanation:
Expand the squared Euclidean norm as the sum of squared moduli of the entries and split the sum
over the product index set $d \times d$ into an iterated sum (`EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq`,
`Fintype.sum_prod_type`). For a fixed $i$, the inner sum over $j$ has a single nonvanishing term,
at $j = i$, contributing $|(\sigma_i : \mathbb{C})|^{2} = \sigma_i^{2}$ because $\sigma_i$ is real;
all other terms are $0$. Summing over $i$ gives the stated identity.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.permutationMatrix_mem_unitary
natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite set with decidable equality and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\iota$.
The associated permutation matrix over $\mathbb{C}$ - the $0/1$ matrix that permutes the standard
basis vectors according to $\sigma$ - lies in the unitary group $U(\iota)$, i.e. it satisfies
$M M^{\dagger} = I$ (equivalently $M^{\dagger}M = I$).
explanation:
Membership in the unitary group unfolds to $M\,M^{\dagger} = I$
(`Matrix.mem_unitaryGroup_iff`). Since a permutation matrix has real $0/1$ entries, its conjugate
transpose is the permutation matrix of the inverse permutation
(`Matrix.conjTranspose_permMatrix`), and the product of two permutation matrices is the permutation
matrix of the composite (`Matrix.permMatrix_mul`). Composing $\sigma$ with $\sigma^{-1}$ yields the
identity permutation, whose permutation matrix is $I$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.exists_proofUniversalHarmonicCatalyst
theorem_title: Universal embezzlement: one harmonic catalyst produces every target state by local unitaries
natural_language_statement:
Fix a dimension $d \ge 1$ and an accuracy $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there exists $n \ge 1$ with the
following universal property: for **every** bipartite unit vector
$\xi \in \mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{d}$ there are unitaries $U, V$ on $\mathbb{C}^{dn}$ with
$$\bigl\|\,(U \otimes V)\,|\mu_{dn}\rangle \;-\; \xi \otimes |\mu_{n}\rangle\,\bigr\| \;\le\;
\varepsilon,$$
where $|\mu_N\rangle$ is the normalized harmonic (embezzlement) state on
$\mathbb{C}^{N}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{N}$ and the right-hand side is read inside
$\mathbb{C}^{dn}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{dn}$ via the regrouping $\mathbb{C}^{dn} \cong \mathbb{C}^{d}
\otimes \mathbb{C}^{n}$ applied to each party's system. The essential point is the order of the
quantifiers: $n$ depends only on $d$ and $\varepsilon$, not on the target $\xi$. So a single shared
resource state lets two spatially separated players create any $d \times d$ entangled state to
within $\varepsilon$ using local unitaries alone, while returning the catalyst essentially intact.
explanation:
Put $\delta = \min(\varepsilon^{2}/2,\,1)$ and use `exists_proofHarmonicNumber_ratio_ge` to choose
$n \ge 1$ with $1 - \delta \le H_{n}/H_{dn}$, where $H_N$ is the $N$-th harmonic number; this
quantifies the well-known slow, near scale-invariant growth of $H_N$ and is where universality in
$\xi$ comes from, since $n$ is fixed before $\xi$ is seen. Given $\xi$, take a Schmidt decomposition
$\xi = (U_0 \otimes V_0)|\psi_\sigma\rangle$ with nonnegative coefficients satisfying
$\sum_i \sigma_i^{2} = 1$ (`exists_proofUnitSchmidtDecomposition`), and take
$U = \tilde U_0 P$, $V = \tilde V_0 P$, where $\tilde{\cdot}$ lifts a unitary on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$ to
$\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{n} \cong \mathbb{C}^{dn}$ by tensoring with the identity and $P$
is the permutation unitary that reorders the computational basis into descending harmonic order.
The diagonal case is the analytic core: `universalDiagonalCatalyst_distance` gives
$\|(P\otimes P)|\mu_{dn}\rangle - |\psi_\sigma\rangle\otimes|\mu_n\rangle\| \le \sqrt{2\delta}$ from
the harmonic ratio bound. The general case follows because local unitaries are isometries and
intertwine the two targets, $(\tilde U_0 \otimes \tilde V_0)(|\psi_\sigma\rangle\otimes|\mu_n\rangle)
= \xi \otimes |\mu_n\rangle$ (`harmonicTargetLift_diagonal_action`); finally
$\sqrt{2\delta} \le \varepsilon$ by the choice of $\delta$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.targetReducedDensity_posSemidef
theorem_title: The reduced density matrix of a bipartite unit vector is positive semidefinite
natural_language_statement:
Let $\xi \in \mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{d}$ be a bipartite unit vector with coefficients
$\xi_{a,b}$, and let $C(\xi)$ be its coefficient matrix, $C(\xi)_{b,a} = \xi_{a,b}$. Then the
matrix
$$C(\xi)^{\dagger}C(\xi), \qquad \bigl(C(\xi)^{\dagger}C(\xi)\bigr)_{a,a'} \;=\;
\sum_{b}\overline{\xi_{a,b}}\,\xi_{a',b},$$
is positive semidefinite. This matrix is the Gram matrix of the columns of $C(\xi)$; up to
transposition it is the reduced density matrix of $\xi$ on the first tensor factor. Normalization
of $\xi$ is not used for positivity; it only makes the trace equal to $1$.
explanation:
Immediate from the general fact that $A^{\dagger}A$ is positive semidefinite for any complex matrix
$A$ (`Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self`), applied to $A = C(\xi)$: it is Hermitian, and for
any vector $v$ one has $v^{\dagger}A^{\dagger}Av = \|Av\|^{2} \ge 0$.

name: QuantumParallelRepetition.dSVSoftBobLeftReducedDensity_posSemidef
theorem_title: Bob's reduced density matrix of a bipartite unit vector is positive semidefinite
natural_language_statement:
Let $\zeta \in \mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{d}$ be a bipartite unit vector with coefficients
$\zeta_{a,b}$, and let $C(\zeta)$ be its coefficient matrix, $C(\zeta)_{b,a} = \zeta_{a,b}$. Then
the matrix
$$C(\zeta)\,C(\zeta)^{\dagger}, \qquad \bigl(C(\zeta)C(\zeta)^{\dagger}\bigr)_{b,b'} \;=\;
\sum_{a}\zeta_{a,b}\,\overline{\zeta_{a,b'}},$$
is positive semidefinite. This is the Gram matrix of the rows of $C(\zeta)$, i.e. the reduced
density matrix of $\zeta$ on the second (Bob) tensor factor; it is the companion of the
corresponding statement for $C(\zeta)^{\dagger}C(\zeta)$ on the other factor, and the two matrices
have the same nonzero spectrum.
explanation:
Immediate from the general fact that $A A^{\dagger}$ is positive semidefinite for any complex
matrix $A$ (`Matrix.posSemidef_self_mul_conjTranspose`), applied to $A = C(\zeta)$: it is
Hermitian, and for any vector $v$ one has $v^{\dagger}AA^{\dagger}v = \|A^{\dagger}v\|^{2} \ge 0$.
